name: Kingdom of Poland and Grand Duchy of Lithuania
summary: The medieval Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, joined by a personal union in 1386 under the Jagiellonian dynasty, before forming the Commonwealth in 1569.

knownFor.label: Battle of Grunwald
knownFor.note: Poland and Lithuania defeated the Teutonic Knights.

knownFor.label: Jagiellonian University
knownFor.note: Founded in Kraków; Copernicus studied there.

location.value: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania covered Lithuania, Belarus, most of Ukraine and parts of Latvia. The Kingdom of Poland was the Polish Crown lands.
location.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)

terrain.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

climate.value: Continental, with cold winters and warm summers.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

resources.value: Grain, timber, salt (the Wieliczka mine) and furs.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

disasters.value: The Black Death was relatively mild in Poland.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

population.value: Lithuania: about 400,000 people in 1260 (68% ethnic Lithuanians), 2.5 million in 1430 (infobox). The page gives no figure for Poland around 1340.
population.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)

urbanisation.value: Kraków, Vilnius, Gdańsk and Lviv were the main cities.
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

disease.value: Plague outbreaks occurred in the 1300s and later.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

migration.value: Jewish and German settlers were welcomed and built towns.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

economicBase.value: Not described for the grain trade; the pages mention only Vytautas's economic reforms.

tradeRoutes.value: Baltic grain exports through Gdańsk to the Netherlands and western Europe.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

wealth.value: Growing wealth from grain and timber exports, especially for the nobles.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

moneyAndTax.value: Silver coins such as the grosz, and nobles often paid few taxes.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

inequality.value: Nobles gained privileges; peasants increasingly bound to land.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

governmentType.value: A personal union under the Union of Krewo; the pages date it to August 1385 or 1386 (the body and infobox disagree). Poland was a monarchy and Lithuania a grand duchy.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569) (checked 13 Nov 2026)

keyRulers.value: Bolesław I Chrobry, first crowned king of Poland in 1025; Jadwiga, who married Jagiełło; Jogaila (Władysław II Jagiełło); and Vytautas, regent 1392–1401 and grand duke 1401–30, under whom Lithuania reached its greatest extent. Casimir III is not on these pages.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569) (checked 13 Nov 2026)

succession.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

institutions.value: Union of Krewo: 14 August 1385 in the infobox but 1386 in the text; Union of Lublin on 1 July 1569 created the Commonwealth.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)

stability.value: Generally stable under the Jagiellonian dynasty, with wars on the borders.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

eliteConflict.value: Nobles gained privileges from kings in return for support, such as the Nihil novi act (1505).
eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

armyAndTech.value: Heavy cavalry and levies of nobles, with famous victories at Grunwald (1410).
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

majorWars.value: Battle of Grunwald (1410): a decisive Polish–Lithuanian victory over the Teutonic Order, with Vytautas commanding the Grand Duchy’s forces.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)

territoryChange.value: Lithuania stretched to the Black Sea under Vytautas.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

alliancesRivals.value: United by the Union of Krewo (1385); rivals were the Teutonic Order, Muscovy and the Crimean Tatars.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

inventions.value: Few major inventions; Copernicus, educated in Kraków, worked here.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

scienceEducation.value: The Kraków Academy was founded in 1364, later the Jagiellonian University, where Copernicus studied.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

openness.value: Religious tolerance was relatively high, with Catholics, Orthodox, Jews, Muslims and Protestants living together.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

communicationTransport.value: Rivers and trade roads linked the Baltic to the Black Sea.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

religion.value: Lithuanian nobles followed a polytheistic religion until 1387, when Lithuania converted to Catholicism; most Ruthenian lands stayed Orthodox. Catholicism was Poland's state religion.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania and Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569) (checked 13 Nov 2026)

languageWriting.value: Polish, Lithuanian, Ruthenian and Latin were all used.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

artsArchitecture.value: Gothic churches, the Wawel Castle in Kraków and the Gdańsk merchant houses.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

sharedIdentity.value: Loyalty to the dynasty and the nobility, with the Catholic Church shaping Polish identity.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

dailyLife.value: Wooden village houses; bread, kasha, beer.
dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

colonisation.value: None; the union grew by treaty and conquest in Eastern Europe.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

riseSignals.value: The Grand Duchy of Lithuania existed from the 13th century; Mindaugas was crowned on 6 July 1253.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)

peakPeriod.value: By 1440 the grand duchy was the largest European state, about 930,000 km² in 1430.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)

declineSignals.value: No decline as such: the realm became the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth in 1569.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Kingdom of Poland (1385–1569); Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania

outcome.value: The Third Partition of 24 October 1795 divided the territory among Russia, Prussia and Austria.
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Grand Duchy of Lithuania (checked 13 Nov 2026)
